brief.what_it_is: A reference C implementation of the LZFSE compression algorithm, Apple's Lempel-Ziv style codec that uses Finite State Entropy coding. It ships as a library (liblzfse.a with lzfse.h) plus a command-line tool called lzfse. The README does not show the tool's input and output syntax, so the exact CLI usage is not confirmed from these pages.
brief.why_it_exists: The README says LZFSE targets similar compression rates to deflate (zlib) at higher compression and decompression speed. It presents the project as a reference implementation of the compressor Apple introduced in its Compression library with OS X 10.11 and iOS 9.
brief.how_it_works: LZFSE is a Lempel-Ziv style algorithm that finds repeated byte sequences, then uses Finite State Entropy coding to encode the result. The source tree separates the pieces: lzfse_encode*.c and lzfse_decode*.c for the LZFSE entry points, lzfse_fse.c for the entropy coder, and lzvn_encode_base.c and lzvn_decode_base.c for a separate LZVN codec in the same tree.

entry.title: lzfse
entry.tldr: Apple's open-sourced LZFSE compressor in plain C, pairing Lempel-Ziv matching with Finite State Entropy coding for zlib-like ratios at higher speed.
entry.deeper_look:
lzfse is the reference C implementation of the compressor Apple introduced in its Compression library with OS X 10.11 and iOS 9. It ships as a small library (`liblzfse.a` and `lzfse.h`) plus a command-line tool called `lzfse`. The README calls LZFSE "a Lempel-Ziv style data compression algorithm using Finite State Entropy coding" and says it targets "similar compression rates at higher compression and decompression speed compared to deflate using zlib."

The idea underneath is the two-stage split common to modern compressors. First, an LZ pass finds repeated byte sequences and replaces them with references. Then an entropy coder squeezes the result. Here the entropy stage is Finite State Entropy, a table-driven coder that stands in for the Huffman step used in deflate. That pairing is how the design aims for zlib-level ratios at better speed.

The source tree is small enough to read in an afternoon, and it is laid out to show the seams. `lzfse_encode*.c` and `lzfse_decode*.c` hold the LZFSE entry points, `lzfse_fse.c` holds the entropy coder, and `lzvn_encode_base.c` and `lzvn_decode_base.c` hold LZVN, a separate codec that lives in the same tree. Most people meet zlib or zstd; this is a rare chance to read a production codec that came out of Apple.

entry.whats_unique: It is an Apple-authored codec released as a clean C reference, in a field where most people only ever meet zlib or zstd. LZVN, a second Apple codec, sits in the same source tree.
entry.caveats: The README is brief, with no CLI examples or benchmarks, and its build notes are old (tested on Ubuntu 15.10 with gcc 5.2.1), so the project's current maintenance status is unclear.
